title: Repository map
summary: One monorepo holds the PHP control plane, the Go data plane, the Node adapter services, the React apps and the device firmware. They share no generated code across languages: each one reads the same files in contracts/ and tests against the same fixtures.

boxes.label: apps/api
boxes.detail: The control plane. Code is grouped by domain under app/Domain, each with its own routes, models and services. The same image runs the API, every queue worker and the scheduler.

boxes.label: deploy/ and tooling/
boxes.detail: deploy/ holds the development and release Compose files, the Dockerfiles and the host playbook. tooling/ holds bootstrap, the release tool, simulators and the verification scripts that drive a running stack. ./taskw is the entry point to both.

boxes.label: services/runtime
boxes.detail: One Go module with three commands: runtime, broker-admin and committed-consumer. The single image carries all three, plus a copy of contracts/ for its contract registry.

boxes.label: firmware/
boxes.detail: The device SDK with its ports (ESP-IDF, FreeRTOS, MCUXpresso, POSIX) and the starter kits. The API image packages both, so the API can hand a device its starter kit. The SDK's tests replay the shared Sparkplug fixtures.

boxes.label: contracts/
boxes.detail: JSON Schemas with golden fixtures, the pinned Sparkplug protobuf, the unit catalogue and the exported OpenAPI description. There is no generated contracts package: PHP, Go, TypeScript, Python and C tests read these files directly, so a change that breaks one language fails that language's suite.

boxes.label: services/adapters
boxes.detail: One Dockerfile with three targets: the adapter manager that starts tenant runtimes, the public webhook receiver, and the tenant runtime image with the platform's Node-RED nodes.

boxes.label: apps/portal, apps/admin
boxes.detail: The tenant portal and the platform admin app. Both depend on the workspace packages rather than on each other; the portal also uses charts and the workflow editor.

boxes.label: packages/
boxes.detail: Shared TypeScript: the design-system kit (ui), chart builders (charts), the typed API client, shared account screens (auth), the automation editor (workflow-editor) and the SDK for external applications (integration-sdk). A change here means rebuilding both web apps.

boxes.label: Other apps
boxes.detail: The public landing page and developer docs, the component gallery, this atlas, and a demo application built on the integration SDK. All use the ui kit.

steps.text: Start in the middle. contracts/ is plain files: schemas, fixtures that must validate against them, and the Sparkplug protobuf.
Laravel reads them from the checkout locally and from a copy inside its image, and exports the OpenAPI description back into contracts/.
The Go runtime carries its own copy and its tests fail when its messages drift from the schemas.
TypeScript tests read the same fixtures, for example the panel suggestions that the portal and Laravel must rank identically.
The embedded SDK replays the Sparkplug fixtures, so device code and the runtime decoder agree on the bytes.
A Python checker validates every fixture against its schema, and a script generates the simulators' Sparkplug bindings from the proto.
The web apps share code only through workspace packages. A change in packages/ means rebuilding both the portal and admin.
Dockerfiles in deploy/ build each app and service from the repository root, which is why an image can include contracts/ and firmware/.
